title: JSPS Invitational Fellowship for Research in Japan (Short-term)
description: A short-term research fellowship run by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), a Japanese government-affiliated funding agency, inviting researchers based outside Japan to conduct collaborative research at a Japanese university or research institution for 14 to 60 days, in any field (natural sciences, social sciences, or humanities). JSPS covers a round-trip economy-class flight, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day (approximately USD 120/day at recent exchange rates -- treat the USD figure as an estimate, since JSPS publishes the amount only in yen), a research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000 (approximately USD 1,000), and overseas travel insurance. Applicants must be citizens of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan, and either hold a doctoral degree obtained within the last six years, or hold a position equivalent to university professor, associate professor, or assistant professor in Japan (which covers researchers whose doctorate is older than six years). A Japanese host researcher and institution must be identified and involved in the application, which is submitted through that host institution rather than by the applicant alone. This is the call for fellowships starting between 1 April 2027 and 31 March 2028; the application deadline is 28 August 2026, 17:00 Japan Standard Time. JSPS runs this fellowship call every fiscal year.
org: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
visaNote: This is short-term research collaboration, not employment; short-term visitor visa arrangements depend on nationality and are typically supported by the host institution in Japan.

title: ASEAN Scholar Fellowship (CDRI)
description: A five-month research fellowship at the Cambodia Development Resource Institute (CDRI), Cambodia's leading independent development-policy think tank, based in Phnom Penh. Fellows spend three months in residence at CDRI working closely with its researchers, followed by two months of remote collaboration to finish research outputs (working papers, policy briefs, or methodological guides) and maintain the institutional connection. CDRI provides a fellowship stipend (amount not published on the official fellowship page), office space, and full access to CDRI's research facilities, library, computing resources, and data infrastructure. Aimed at mid- to senior-level researchers, and open to citizens of ASEAN member states other than Cambodia (to support cross-border regional research collaboration). Applications require a CV, a one-page motivation letter, a letter of recommendation from the applicant's current institution, and a concrete collaborative research proposal relevant to Cambodia and/or ASEAN development priorities. Application deadline: 15 August 2026, submitted by email to CDRI.
visaNote: This is a short-term research fellowship, not employment; ASEAN nationals should confirm Cambodia's visa-on-arrival/e-visa requirements for a multi-month stay well ahead of the residency start.
